clue.text: One-time player-such a demanding guy!

parts.note: one-time means former, abbreviated as ex
a player on stage is an actor

explanation.surface: A former stage performer turns out to be a very demanding man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who extorts or insists on payment or obedience is a demanding person.

clue.text: Solitary before time changed him

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of time are rearranged here

explanation.surface: A loner whose life was transformed by the passing years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns TIME into MITE, which follows ERE. 'Solitary' is a noun here, a person living alone; 'him' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary, as a noun, is a recluse or hermit, which is what this religious hermit is.

clue.text: Meet a sailor going around the shore

indicators.note: going around means the pair of pieces surround the support inside them

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman, a sailor
a shore is a prop or support for a wall

explanation.surface: A seaman walks around the coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shore' suggests the coast, but it is a supporting beam. 'Meet' is the old adjective meaning fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet in its old sense means suitable or fitting, as does this word meaning relevant.

clue.text: Not relaxed, having drunk rather too much

explanation.surface: Someone tense after drinking a bit too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense and taut on one side; slangily intoxicated on the other.

clue.text: He will set one right concerning kitchen furniture

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
a dresser is a kitchen cabinet with shelves

explanation.surface: A man promises to sort out a problem about the kitchen cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: One who puts a wrong right gives remedy for it.

clue.text: Get the small child more suitable reading-matter

parts.note: ch is the abbreviation for child
apter is the comparative of apt, meaning suitable

explanation.surface: Find a youngster something better to read.
explanation.definitionFit: A section of a book is a portion of reading material.

clue.text: A youngster undergoing training acted badly

indicators.note: badly tells us the letters of acted are put in a poor order

explanation.surface: A trainee gave a poor performance on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A young trainee in the armed forces or police is a cadet.

clue.text: Transport the general public aren't fit to use

definitions.text: Transport the general public aren't fit to use

parts.words: Transport the general public aren't fit to use
parts.note: a vehicle used by people who are unwell or injured, not those who are fit and healthy

explanation.surface: A vehicle that ordinary people are not allowed to ride.
explanation.definitionFit: This emergency vehicle carries the sick and injured, so it is used by those who are not fit.

clue.text: First trainee taken into the plant

indicators.note: taken into means the pieces go inside the word the

parts.note: first is 1st, written as IST
L is the learner plate, a trainee

explanation.surface: The first apprentice is brought into the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: IST (1ST, the figure 1 read as I) plus L go inside THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickly weed with purple flowers is a plant, and Scotland's emblem.

clue.text: Back up rebel leader, way-out

indicators.note: leader picks out the first letter of rebel

parts.note: an egress is a way out or exit

explanation.surface: Support the leader of the rebellion and the escape route.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back or revert to an earlier state is to move backwards.

clue.text: The shifty grandee caused exasperation

indicators.note: shifty suggests the letters of grandee shift around

explanation.surface: A dodgy nobleman annoyed people.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made someone furious is to have caused exasperation.

clue.text: Calling for the waterproofing of footwear

explanation.surface: A demand for boots to be waterproofed.
explanation.definitionFit: Naming someone or something; also applying dubbin, a grease that waterproofs leather boots.

clue.text: It could be apt in time to appear irritable

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of apt in time may become something else

explanation.surface: Being punctual might seem a sign of irritability.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless and short-tempered with delay is synonymous with irritable.

clue.text: Turner put many articles together

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, many
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A painter assembled numerous items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter, but it is a machine that turns wood or metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine for shaping material by rotating it turns things.

clue.text: A canvas support

parts.note: the frame that holds a painter's canvas upright while working

explanation.definitionFit: An artist's stand holds a canvas as it is painted.

clue.text: A yobbo must accept a woman's attacks

indicators.note: must accept means the yobbo takes the next pieces inside him

parts.note: a lout is a yobbo, a hooligan
she's is a woman's, she is

explanation.surface: A thug has to take a woman's assaults.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike out violently at someone means assaults on them.

clue.text: Back the head's strict attitude

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship
a ness is a headland, a head

explanation.surface: Turn the headmaster's severe manner around.
explanation.definitionFit: Severity of manner is a strict attitude.

clue.text: Making a list seen as vital

indicators.note: making suggests the letters of a list seen are made into something new

explanation.surface: Drawing up a list is regarded as crucial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indispensable is vital.

clue.text: Journalists divided about incontestable obligations

indicators.note: divided about means the press is split around another word

parts.note: the press means journalists collectively
sure means certain, incontestable

explanation.surface: Reporters split over undeniable duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Demands and constraints that weigh on someone are obligations.

clue.text: Have to get the sheriff's men onto a ship

parts.note: a posse is a band of men called up by a sheriff
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A lawman's team must board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have it.

clue.text: Offer a lift

parts.note: reads like proposing a ride in a car, but means raise something up

explanation.definitionFit: To raise or hoist something up gives it a lift.

clue.text: Keen to take silver in always

indicators.note: in places the metal inside the poetic word for always

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Always ready to accept some silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enthusiastic and impatient for something is being keen.

clue.text: Tearing about to find a certain type of stone

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of tearing are moved around

explanation.surface: Rushing around in search of a particular rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard igneous rock used in building is a type of stone.

clue.text: Joints where jackets are required

explanation.surface: Places where coats must be worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cannabis cigarettes; also short double-breasted coats worn by sailors.

clue.text: Viewed, so it's said, as disagreement

indicators.note: so it's said tells us the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: seen means viewed

explanation.surface: Observed, reportedly, as a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a public fuss or row is an angry disagreement.

clue.text: Count the money with grim consequences

parts.note: L is the sign for pounds, money
and means with, in addition
grave means grim, with serious consequences

explanation.surface: Tallying the cash has dire results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb, but it is a German nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A German count with territorial rule held this noble title.

clue.text: A service held by the French in Ulster

indicators.note: held by means the pieces go inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
RN, the Royal Navy, is an armed service

explanation.surface: A church service conducted by French people in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The service looks religious; it is the Royal Navy. LARNE is a port town in Ulster, Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A port town of County Antrim lies in the province of Ulster.

clue.text: A king, and so majestic

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A monarch, and therefore regal.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressive and stately in scale is majestic.

clue.text: To charm some women a mournful look is best

indicators.note: some tells us only part of the words women a mournful is used

explanation.surface: To win over certain women, a sad expression works best.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone fall in love is to charm them.

clue.text: Fancy a copy with lining in

indicators.note: lining means the word in lines the inside of the copy

parts.note: an image is a copy or likeness

explanation.surface: Like a duplicate with an inner layer.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose or picture something in the mind is to fancy it.

clue.text: Spirit creates respect

indicators.note: creates suggests the letters of respect are made into a new word

explanation.surface: A ghost commands esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost or phantom is a spirit.

clue.text: People putting up with others

parts.note: reads as tolerant folk, but means tenants staying in someone else's house

explanation.definitionFit: Paying tenants stay in rooms in another person's home.
